symptom: `alter entity E drop attribute "A"`, `drop entity E` and `drop association X` passed `check` (with or without --references) when a microflow, nanoflow, page or snippet still used the target; `exec` applied the drop with at most a "may still reference" warning (`drop entity` printed nothing) and `mx check` then reported CE1613 on each user (CE0161 where the attribute was only in an XPath).
file: mdl/executor/validate_dropped_member_references.go CheckDroppedMemberReferences (MDL108), called from cmd/mxcli/cmd_check.go in the catalog-backed tier. Tests: validate_dropped_member_references_test.go
cause: CheckEntityMemberDrops (MDL087) only reports members a `create or modify` loses without being asked; an explicit drop is excluded by intent, and nothing asked who else uses the dropped member. The catalog already holds the answer (`show references to`).
insight: **The reference graph is the whole rule; the work is deciding what NOT to report.** Measured one project per case on MxBuild 11.16.1: microflow, nanoflow, page and snippet users are CE1613, an XPath-only user is CE0161, dropping an entity that only an association points at is clean (the association goes with it), and dropping then re-adding the attribute is clean. So the rule reads only those four source types, ignores documents the script itself drops, creates or alters (it may fix the reference), skips a member the script puts back, and opens the FULL catalog (references are not in fast mode) only when the script has such a drop. `exec` still applies the drop: the project tier is check-only, like MDL087, so refusing there is a separate decision.
